problem: Multi-hop QA needs coordinated relational and textual evidence across reasoning steps; graph-augmented RAG uses a pre-built/query-updated graph, KGQA systems search topic-centered subgraphs, and memory-augmented agents evolve memory without reconciling graph and text - each addresses only part of the loop.
method: Co-E is a training-free system built on synchronized bidirectional graph-text working memory: a synchronization cycle consolidates textual memory, extracts relational triples into graph memory, and injects graph facts back into the generation context, so both memories shape subsequent retrieval and generation.
key_assumptions: Textual and relational evidence must revise each other during reasoning.
Triples extracted from retrieved text can be trusted as graph memory without a repair loop.
A training-free system can be competitive with trained systems.
A pre-existing KG is not required (graph memory is built from text).
main_contribution: A training-free co-evolving graph-text memory system for multi-hop QA that synchronizes textual and relational working memory bidirectionally during reasoning; code released.
datasets: six multi-hop QA benchmarks (names not enumerated in the abstract; full text mentions Wikidata-scale evaluation)
results: Co-E improves over comparable training-free open-backbone baselines and is competitive with larger or trained systems on six multi-hop QA benchmarks.
limitations: Training-free: no learned supervision, so gains may not transfer to a fine-tuned model setting.
Noisy edges and incomplete paths require the memory synchronization to correct them at inference; no offline repair.
No hop-depth breakdown reported in the abstract.
code_availability: Codebase stated in full text: https://github.com/hieum98/wemg (repository could not be inspected: GitHub tools unavailable).

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: Co-E is training-free inference-time memory synchronization between text and graph; it never trains the model on triples or context-enriched supervision, has no repair loop, and does not study hop-depth transfer. It shares the premise that surrounding relational context matters for multi-hop reasoning but implements it as dynamic retrieval rather than supervision.
relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap moderate: both concern multi-hop reasoning with graph and text evidence. Method overlap moderate: both build triple/graph context around a query, but Co-E's memory is updated at inference and pairs text with graph, whereas the idea fixes supervision examples offline. Evaluation overlap low-moderate: six multi-hop QA benchmarks vs the idea's MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ, and no training-regime comparison.
